# YarGPT

> YarGPT runs personal AI agents, called bots, on your own computer. Each bot is a Claude Code CLI session with its own chat, memory, routines and working folder. Bots can work together in group chats, called rooms, and can message each other. There is no cloud service: the server, the SQLite database and the bots all run locally.

This is the full reference for YarGPT. The short index is at <https://yargpt.com/llms.txt>.

## What YarGPT is

- A Go server with a web UI. Each time a bot works, the server runs the Claude Code CLI (`claude`) on your machine with your Claude account. YarGPT adds the chats, memory, schedules, approvals, rooms and bot-to-bot messages around it.
- It runs on macOS and Linux. It needs Claude Code CLI 2.1.319 or later, signed in, with `claude` on `PATH`.
- The web UI is at <http://127.0.0.1:7777>. All data is in `~/.yargpt`.
- On a Mac, an app can run the server in the background from login on, with one menu-bar item, **Exit server**. The server log is then `~/Library/Logs/YarGPT/server.log`.
- YarGPT has no login. Use it only on a computer that one person uses (see "Security").

## Bots and turns

- A bot has a name (at most 80 characters) and instructions (at most 8000 characters). It works in its own folder, `~/.yargpt/bots/<bot id>`. The bot id is the last part of the chat address, `/chat/<bot id>`.
- A new bot starts and introduces itself in its chat.
- Each piece of work is a turn. A turn starts from a message of yours, a routine, a message from another bot, a room post, a compaction, a bot's first start, or a background task that reported.
- A bot runs one turn at a time. Other turns wait in its queue. Across all bots, at most 3 turns run at the same time (`-max-parallel`).
- A bot's turns share one Claude Code session, which each turn resumes. In each room, a member has a separate session.
- The model's plain text is private. You see only what the bot sends with the `send_to_user` tool. When a turn ends without a message, the chat shows the model's final text, marked as a fallback.
- A bot can start a long command in the background and keep talking. The chat lists the running tasks, and **Stop** ends them.
- When a turn reaches your Claude account's usage limit, YarGPT starts no new turns until the limit resets. Turns that already run continue.
- After a restart of the server, turns that were running are marked interrupted, open approval cards expire, and background tasks are gone.

### Messages and files

- A message has at most 32000 characters.
- A message can carry up to 4 files, 100 MB in total. Images: PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, up to 10 MB each. Videos: MP4, WebM or QuickTime, up to 50 MB each.
- Bots can send images and videos too. A bot's file must be in its working folder, the media folder or a temp folder such as `/tmp`.
- Commands at the start of a message:
  - `/clear` starts a fresh conversation context. The chat stays visible.
  - `/compact` shortens the context and shows the token counts before and after.
  - `/<skill> <request>` runs a skill now.

## Approvals

- A bot reads files and searches the web without asking. Before it runs a command, changes a file or calls a connector tool, it shows an approval card.
- **Allow once** lets this one call run. **Always allow <tool>** lets this bot use that tool without asking from now on. **Deny** stops the call.
- A card expires after 10 minutes without an answer, or when the bot stops working.
- To remove an "always allow" permission, open the bot panel, then **Settings**, then **Always allowed tools**.
- In the sidebar, a shield marks a bot that waits for an approval. A question bubble marks a bot that asked you something.

## Memory

- Two scopes:
  - `agent`: the bot's own memory.
  - `user`: facts about you, shared with every bot ("Shared with all bots" in the UI).
- Three tiers:
  - `profile`: always in mind. The bot sees these facts on every turn ("Always in mind" in the UI).
  - `log`: the journal, with dates. The bot searches it when it needs to. This is the default tier.
  - `note`: a short-term note that expires after 7 days.
- A fact is one sentence of at most 500 characters.
- Each fact records who wrote it: you or a bot. A bot treats a standing rule as yours only when you wrote the fact.
- Bots save facts on their own. You can see, add and delete facts in the bot panel under **Memory**.
- Rooms have no memory of their own.

## Routines

- A routine is a prompt and a schedule. A bot creates one when you ask for something that repeats, for example "every weekday at 8:10, brief me on my calendar".
- A schedule is a 5-field cron expression in your local time zone, or `@hourly`, `@daily`, `@weekly` or `@every <duration>`, for example `@every 2h`.
- Two runs must be at least 5 minutes apart. A bot can have at most 50 routines. A routine prompt has at most 8000 characters.
- The **Routines** tab shows each routine and its next run. There you can pause it, run it now or delete it. When you change a routine, the bot gets a notice.
- Routines start only on a schedule. Routines that start on events are not built yet.

## Skills

- A skill is a saved procedure that every bot can use. It is a `SKILL.md` file in `~/.yargpt/skills/<skill id>/`.
- The skill id comes from its name: lowercase letters and digits, joined by hyphens, at most 64 characters. A description has at most 1000 characters, and the body at most 64000.
- A bot can save a process that you will repeat as a skill. A new skill is available from the bot's next turn.
- The **Skills** tab lists the skills. To run one now, type `/<skill> <request>` in a bot's chat.

## Rooms

A room is a group chat with you and one or more bots. To create one, click **+** next to **Rooms**, give the room a name, and choose its members. A room needs at least 1 member, and a room cannot be a member of another room.

Who wakes up:

- Your message wakes the members that it @mentions. A message without mentions wakes all members.
- `@here` mentions every member. It must be a word of its own: `me@here.com` and `@hereford` do not count.
- An @mention is `@` followed by the member's name, in any case. Type `@` in the message box to complete a name.
- A bot's post wakes only the members that it @mentions. A post never wakes the bot that wrote it.

How members answer:

- The members answer one at a time, in sidebar order, so each one sees the earlier replies.
- A member that is busy elsewhere answers when it is free.
- Each member keeps its own Claude Code session for the room. On its first turn in a room, a member sees the last 30 messages. On later turns, it sees the messages that it has not seen yet.
- During a turn in a room, the `send_to_user` tool posts into the room, for you and every member.
- A bot can also post into a room that it is in from any turn, with `send_to_agent` and the room's id. A room post always lands at once and can carry files.
- A bot reads older room messages with the `read_room` tool.

Bots can hand work to each other in a room. For example, an Implementer bot @mentions a Reviewer, the Reviewer @mentions a Fixer, and the Fixer @mentions a Merger.

## Bots that message each other

- A bot sends a direct message to another bot with the `send_to_agent` tool. Each bot's prompt lists the other bots and the rooms it is in, with their ids.
- `priority: true` wakes the other bot at once. It gets a turn marked `[agent]`, which tells it that the message comes from a bot, not from you.
- Without priority, the message waits until that bot's next turn.
- Both chats show the message.
- A direct message is text only, 1 to 8000 characters. Files can go only to a room. A bot cannot message itself.
- Messages are asynchronous, like texting. A reply, if any, arrives later as its own turn. Bots are told to reply only when they have something to add, so they do not trade acknowledgements.
- Hop limit: after 6 bot-to-bot messages in a row, the next message wakes no one. A priority message then waits for the bot's next turn, and a room post wakes no one. The limit covers direct messages and room @mentions. It stops bots from keeping each other busy forever.

## Bot tools

Each `claude` process connects to YarGPT's MCP endpoint, `/mcp`, with a bearer token that is valid only for its turn. The bots use these tools. They are not for external clients.

- `send_to_user`: send a message to the user. This is the only output the user sees. In a room turn, it posts into the room.
  - `text`: markdown. It can be empty when files are attached.
  - `files`: up to 4 paths of images or videos.
  - `needs_reply`: true when the bot cannot continue without an answer. The app then shows that the bot waits for you.
- `send_to_agent`: message another bot, or post into a room that the bot is in.
  - `target_id`: the id of a bot, or of a room.
  - `message`: at most 8000 characters.
  - `priority`: true wakes the bot now. False delivers at its next turn. Room posts always land at once.
  - `files`: room posts only, up to 4.
- `read_room`: read the latest messages of a room that the bot is in, oldest first.
  - `room_id`.
  - `limit`: 1 to 50, default 20.
  - `before_seq`: page back from the oldest `#seq` that the bot has.
  - Reading does not change what the bot's next room turn shows as new.
- `recall_memory`: search the bot's memory and the shared user memory.
  - `query`: facts that share more words rank first.
  - `scope`: `agent`, `user` or `all` (default).
  - `limit`: 1 to 50, default 20.
- `update_memory`: write or forget a fact.
  - `action`: `write` or `forget`.
  - `fact`: for forget, the exact recorded text.
  - `scope`: `agent` (default) or `user`.
  - `tier`: `profile`, `log` (default) or `note`.
  - `replaces`: the exact text of a fact that the new fact replaces.
- `update_routine`: manage the bot's own routines.
  - `action`: `create`, `update`, `pause`, `resume`, `delete`, `run_now` or `list`.
  - `id`: required except for create and list.
  - `name`, `prompt`, `schedule`: required for create.
- `update_skill`: manage the skills that all bots share.
  - `action`: `write`, `delete` or `list`.
  - `name`, `description`, `body`: required for write.
  - `id`: required for delete.
- `update_profile`: change the bot's own `name` or `instructions`. A field that the bot leaves out stays the same.
- `approve`: internal. Claude Code calls it through `--permission-prompt-tool` to show an approval card.

## Global instructions

Put instructions for every bot in `~/.yargpt/AGENTS.md`, for example:

```markdown
- Never add AI attribution to commits or pull requests.
- Ask me before any merge.
```

- A bot's own instructions win over this file.
- A change reaches a bot when it next starts a Claude Code process.
- Every bot can read the file, so keep tokens out of it.
- A file over 32 KiB stops every bot's turns until you shorten it.
- Your own Claude Code settings, hooks, `CLAUDE.md` files and MCP servers do not reach the bots. Use `AGENTS.md` and `connectors.json` instead.

## Connectors

A connector gives bots the tools of an external MCP server, such as Slack or a wiki. List the servers in `~/.yargpt/connectors.json`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "wiki": {
      "url": "https://wiki.example/mcp",
      "bots": ["<bot id>"]
    },
    "search": {
      "url": "https://search.example/mcp",
      "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer <token>"},
      "bots": ["<bot id>"]
    }
  }
}
```

1. Make the file private: `chmod 600 ~/.yargpt/connectors.json`. The file can hold tokens, so YarGPT does not read it otherwise.
2. Sign in to each server that has no `headers`: click **Connectors** at the bottom of the sidebar, then **Connect**, and sign in on the page that opens. YarGPT uses OAuth 2.1, with dynamic client registration and PKCE.

Rules:

- A server with `headers` gets them on each call. For a server that needs no sign-in, set `"headers": {}`.
- A server name uses only `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`. The name `yargpt` is reserved. A bot calls the server's tools as `mcp__<name>__<tool>`.
- The `url` must use https. Plain http is allowed only for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1`.
- `bots` lists the bots that load the server. It does not hide the tokens from other bots.
- Connector tools go through approval cards. **Always allow** applies to one tool, not to the whole server.
- YarGPT reads the file each time a bot starts a Claude Code process, so a change needs no restart. An invalid file fails the bot's turn with an error that names the problem.
- Sign-in tokens are in `~/.yargpt/oauth/<name>.json`, with mode 0600. YarGPT refreshes them before they expire. **Disconnect** deletes them.
- When a server is not signed in, the bot works without it, and the chat says that the server needs sign-in.
- If you change `-addr`, connect again: the sign-in address contains the port.

A server without dynamic client registration needs a client that you register yourself. All `oauth` fields are optional:

```json
"oauth": {"clientId": "<id>", "clientSecret": "<secret, if any>", "scopes": ["<scope>"], "callbackPort": 3118}
```

With `callbackPort`, the sign-in returns to `http://localhost:<callbackPort>/callback`, as in Claude Code's `.mcp.json`. For example, Slack's MCP server works with Slack's public client for Claude Code, after a Slack workspace admin approves it:

```json
"slack": {
  "url": "https://mcp.slack.com/mcp",
  "oauth": {"clientId": "1601185624273.8899143856786", "callbackPort": 3118},
  "bots": ["<bot id>"]
}
```

## Configuration

Flags of the `yargpt` server:

- `-addr` (default `127.0.0.1:7777`): the listen address. YarGPT refuses an address that is not loopback.
- `-data` (default `~/.yargpt`): the data folder.
- `-claude` (default `claude`): the Claude Code CLI to run.
- `-model` (default: Claude Code's default): the model alias for every bot, for example `sonnet`.
- `-max-parallel` (default `3`): the turns that can run at the same time, across all bots.
- `-login-env` (default off): take the environment, such as `PATH`, from your login shell.
- `-tray` (default off): show the macOS menu-bar icon with **Exit server**.
- `-log` (default none): append the log and all other error output to this file. Without it, they go to stderr.

To set `claude`, `model` or `maxParallel` without flags, put them in `~/.yargpt/config.json`, for example `{"model": "sonnet", "maxParallel": 4}`. A flag wins over the file. YarGPT reads the file only when it starts. If the file is invalid, YarGPT does not start, and the error names the file.

The data folder holds:

- `yargpt.db`: bots, chats, memory and routines (SQLite).
- `bots/<bot id>/`: each bot's working folder.
- `skills/`: the skills that all bots share.
- `media/`: the images and videos of messages.
- `AGENTS.md`, `connectors.json`, `config.json`: your optional settings.
- `oauth/`: connector sign-in tokens.
- `run/`: the MCP configs of running bots, with their per-turn tokens.

## How a turn runs

- The server starts `claude -p` in the bot's working folder and sends the prompt on stdin as stream-json.
- The process runs with `--setting-sources project`, `--strict-mcp-config`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BUNDLED_SKILLS=1` and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS=1`.
- The built-in tools are limited to Task, Bash, Monitor, TaskStop, Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep, WebSearch and Skill.
- YarGPT writes each process's MCP config to a 0600 file in `~/.yargpt/run`, so no token shows in the process list. It removes the file when the process exits.
- Tool calls that need approval reach the `approve` tool through `--permission-prompt-tool`.

## Local HTTP API

The web UI uses this API. It is local and not versioned, so it can change between releases.

Rules for every request:

- The server answers only on a loopback address. A request whose `Host` is not loopback gets 403, to block DNS rebinding.
- A request with an `Origin` header from another origin gets 403, to block cross-site request forgery.
- Every `POST` under `/api/` must have `Content-Type: application/json`, or it gets 415.
- A request body has at most 1 MiB. A message body may also carry its files, up to 100 MB before base64.
- There is no authentication beyond these rules.
- An error is JSON: `{"error": "<message>"}`. Status 400 means invalid input, 404 not found, and 409 a conflict, for example an approval that is no longer pending.

Bots and rooms are the same resource. `kind` is `agent` for a bot and `room` for a room.

Bots:

- `GET /api/bots`: all bots and rooms. Each has `id`, `kind`, `name`, `instructions`, `members` (rooms), `attention` (`approval` or `question`), `running`, `tasks`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`.
- `POST /api/bots` with `{"name", "instructions"}`: create a bot. Returns 201 and the bot.
- `GET /api/bots/{id}`: one bot or room.
- `PATCH /api/bots/{id}` with `{"name"?, "instructions"?}`: change a bot.
- `DELETE /api/bots/{id}`: stop the bot's running turn, then delete it. Returns 204.
- `PUT /api/bots/order` with `{"ids": [...]}`: set the order of one sidebar section, all bots or all rooms. Room members answer in the order of the bots section.

Chats:

- `GET /api/bots/{id}/entries?after=<rev>`: the entries of a chat that changed after `rev`, in `rev` order, at most 1000 at a time. Start with `after=0`.
- `POST /api/bots/{id}/messages` with `{"text", "clientNonce", "media"?}`: send a message to a bot or a room.
  - `clientNonce` is required, 1 to 100 characters, and unique for each message.
  - `media` is a list of base64-encoded files.
  - The response is 202 with `{"turnId", "duplicate": false}`. A repeated `clientNonce` starts no second turn: it returns 200 with the first turn's id and `"duplicate": true`.
- `GET /api/media/{name}`: a file of a message.
- `POST /api/bots/{id}/interrupt`: stop the running turn. Returns `{"stopped": true|false}`.
- `POST /api/bots/{id}/clear`: start a fresh context. Returns 204, or 409 while the bot works or has background tasks.
- `POST /api/bots/{id}/compact`: queue a compaction after the current turn. Returns 202 with `{"queued"}`.

Entries:

- Each entry has `id`, `botId`, `seq` (its place in the chat), `rev`, `kind`, `turnId`, `body` and `createdAt`.
- An entry can change after it is created, for example when an approval is answered. Each change gives it a new, higher `rev`, so update entries by `id`.
- Kinds:
  - `user`: your message. `body` has `text` and `media` (file names for `GET /api/media/{name}`).
  - `bot`: a bot's message. `body` has `text`, `fallback`, `needsReply` and `media`. In a room, it also has `speakerId` and `speakerName`.
  - `agent`: a direct message between bots. `body` has `direction` (`in` or `out`), `peerId`, `peerName`, `text`, `priority`, and for `in`, `held`.
  - `approval`: an approval card. `body` has `tool`, `input`, `status` (`pending`, `allowed`, `denied` or `expired`), `decision`, and in a room `bot`.
  - `event` and `activity`: turn events and the tools that a bot used.

Rooms:

- `POST /api/rooms` with `{"name", "instructions", "memberIds"}`: create a room. Returns 201 and the room.
- `PUT /api/rooms/{id}/members` with `{"memberIds"}`: set the members.
- Send a message to a room with `POST /api/bots/{room id}/messages`.

Memory, routines, approvals and permissions:

- `GET /api/bots/{id}/memory`: the facts that the bot sees. Each has `id`, `scope`, `tier`, `fact`, `learnedBy` (`user` or a bot id) and `createdAt`.
- `POST /api/bots/{id}/memory` with `{"scope", "tier", "fact"}`: add a fact as the user. Returns 204.
- `DELETE /api/memory/{id}`: delete a fact.
- `GET /api/bots/{id}/routines`: the bot's routines. Each has `id`, `botId`, `name`, `prompt`, `schedule`, `enabled`, `nextRunAt`, `lastRunAt`, `lastRunBy` and `createdAt`.
- `POST /api/bots/{id}/routines` with `{"name", "prompt", "schedule"}`: create a routine. Returns 201.
- `PATCH /api/routines/{id}` with `{"name"?, "prompt"?, "schedule"?, "enabled"?}`: change, pause or resume a routine.
- `POST /api/routines/{id}/run`: run a routine now. Returns 202 with `{"turnId"}`.
- `DELETE /api/routines/{id}`: delete a routine.
- `POST /api/approvals/{entry id}` with `{"decision": "once" | "always" | "deny"}`: answer an approval card. Returns 204, or 409 when the card is no longer pending.
- `GET /api/bots/{id}/grants`: the tools that the bot may use without asking.
- `DELETE /api/bots/{id}/grants/{tool}`: remove one of them.

Skills and connectors:

- `GET /api/skills`: the skills, with `id`, `name` and `description`.
- `GET /api/skills/{id}`: one skill, with its `body`.
- `DELETE /api/skills/{id}`: delete a skill.
- `GET /api/connectors`: the connectors from `connectors.json`.
- `POST /api/connectors/{name}/connect`: start a sign-in. Returns `{"url"}` to open in a browser. The sign-in returns to `/oauth/callback`.
- `DELETE /api/connectors/{name}/token`: sign out and delete the tokens.

Event stream:

- `GET /api/events` is a server-sent event stream of every change.
- It starts with `event: hello`. If new turns wait for a usage limit, a `pause` event follows.
- Every other event is a `data:` line with a JSON object. Its `type` is one of:
  - `entry`: an entry was added or changed. It has `botId` and `entry`.
  - `state`: a bot started or stopped working. It has `botId` and `running`.
  - `tasks`: a bot's background tasks changed. It has `botId` and `tasks`.
  - `bots`: the list of bots and rooms changed. Fetch `GET /api/bots` again.
  - `pause`: `pausedUntil` is when turns start again. It is absent when the pause ended.
- A comment line, `: ping`, comes every 20 seconds.
- A client that falls behind is disconnected. After each connect, fetch the entries after the highest `rev` that you have.

Examples:

```sh
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7777/api/bots

curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7777/api/bots/<bot id>/messages \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"text": "@here what is the status?", "clientNonce": "<unique id>"}'

curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:7777/api/bots/<bot id>/entries?after=0'

curl -N http://127.0.0.1:7777/api/events
```

## Security

YarGPT has no login. It is safe only on a computer that one person uses, and only because of these limits:

- It listens on loopback only.
- It rejects requests whose `Host` is not loopback, to block DNS rebinding.
- It rejects requests from another web origin, to block cross-site request forgery.
- It rejects API POST requests whose body is not JSON.

Bots run as your user. An approved command can do anything that you can do, so read each approval card before you allow it.

Bots are not isolated from each other. Reading files needs no approval and has no path limit, so any bot can read `AGENTS.md`, `connectors.json`, the tokens in `oauth/`, and the per-turn tokens of other bots' running processes in `run/`.

Each bot's prompt tells it to treat web pages, files, tool output and other bots' messages as data, not as instructions or approval. A prompt is not an enforced control.

## Not built yet

Routines that start on events (only schedules work now), per-bot Claude Code plugins, a vault for secrets, voice, and bots that run on other machines.
